nodes.summary: Algorithmica is the statement that the complexity classes $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{NP}$ are equal.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a polynomial with natural-number coefficients, $L$ a decision problem, and $S$ a family of samplers, where $S_n$ sends each string $r$ of $p(n)$ random bits to a bitstring $S_n(r)$. The pair $(L, S)$ is hard on average when it is not easy on average: there is no polynomial-time computable function $A$ from bitstrings to booleans such that for every natural number $c$ and all sufficiently large $n$, $A$…

nodes.title: Cryptomania

nodes.summary: Exactly one of the statements Algorithmica, Heuristica, Pessiland, Minicrypt and Cryptomania is true: one of them holds and the other four fail.
nodes.title: Exactly one of Impagliazzo's five worlds holds

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a flat Boolean circuit given as a list of gates, each encoded as a (kind, references) pair, and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{k-1})$ be a list of booleans. The gate values of $C$ on $a$ are the gate values, in order, of the circuit on $k$ inputs obtained by decoding each gate of $C$, evaluated on the assignment that sends input $i$ to $a_i$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of an encoded flat circuit

nodes.summary: For an encoded flat Boolean circuit $C$, a list of booleans $a$ and a natural number $k$, the outputs of $C$ on $a$ are the last $k$ entries of the list of gate values of $C$ on $a$, or the whole list if $C$ has fewer than $k$ gates.
nodes.title: Outputs of an encoded flat circuit

nodes.summary: Let $f$ map $n$-bit strings to bitstrings and let $C$ be an encoded flat Boolean circuit. For an $n$-bit string $x$, the candidate preimage $x'$ consists of the last $n$ gate values of $C$ on input $f(x)$ (all of them if $C$ has fewer than $n$ gates), padded with false to length $n$. The inversion success probability of $C$ against $f$ is the fraction of the $2^n$ strings $x$ for which $f(x') = f(x)$.
nodes.title: Inversion success probability of a circuit

nodes.summary: For a map $G$ from bitstrings to bitstrings (the key generator) and a bitstring $r$ of coins, the key pair of $G$ on $r$ is the pair of bitstrings obtained by decoding $G(r)$ with the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of bitstrings, or the pair of empty bitstrings if this decoding fails.
nodes.title: Key pair produced by a key generator

nodes.summary: Let $G$ (key generation) and $E$ (encryption) be maps from bitstrings to bitstrings, let $C$ be an encoded flat Boolean circuit, let $\ell$ be a polynomial with natural-number coefficients and let $n$ be a natural number. nodes.title: Eavesdropping advantage against a public-key scheme

nodes.summary: A serialized gate of a flat Boolean circuit is a pair $(k, r)$ of a natural number $k$ (the gate kind) and a list $r$ of natural numbers (its references, depending on the kind: an input index, a constant bit, or indices of other gates), in the shared encoding of gates as (kind, references) pairs.
nodes.title: Serialized gates of five-worlds circuits

nodes.summary: Heuristica: `P ≠ NP`, but every NP problem is easy on average for every samplable distribution.
nodes.title: Heuristica

nodes.summary: The following four statements hold. First, if public-key encryption exists, then one-way functions exist. Second, if one-way functions exist, then some decision problem $L$ in NP is hard on average for some samplable distribution: there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a family $S$ of maps $S_n$ from $p(n)$-bit coin strings to bitstrings such that $(p, S)$ is samplable and $L$ is hard on…
nodes.title: Impagliazzo's five worlds

nodes.summary: Minicrypt: one-way functions exist, but public-key cryptography does not.
nodes.title: Minicrypt

nodes.title: One-way functions exist

nodes.summary: Pessiland is the statement that $\mathsf{P} \ne \mathsf{NP}$, that one-way functions do not exist, and that some decision problem $L$ in NP is hard on average for some samplable distribution: there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a family $S$ of maps $S_n$ from $p(n)$-bit coin strings to bitstrings such that $(p, S)$ is samplable and $L$ is hard on average with respect to $S$.
nodes.title: Pessiland

nodes.summary: There are a polynomial $\ell$ with natural-number coefficients and polynomial-time computable functions $G$ (key generation), $E$ (encryption) and $D$ (decryption) on bitstrings with the following two properties. Here tuples are passed to these functions and to circuits through their canonical bitstring encodings, and for a bitstring $r$ the keys $(\mathit{pk}, \mathit{sk})$ are the decoding of $G(r)$ as a pair of…
nodes.title: Public-key encryption exists

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a polynomial with natural-number coefficients and let $S$ be a family of maps $S_n$ from $p(n)$-bit coin strings to bitstrings. The pair $(p, S)$ is samplable when every $S_n(r)$ has length exactly $n$ and some polynomial-time computable function on bitstrings maps the canonical bitstring encoding of every pair $(n, r)$ to $S_n(r)$.
nodes.title: Samplable distributions

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
